directAnswer: Pope St. Gregory III, a Syrian, reigned from 731 to 741. He condemned iconoclasm at Roman synods, strengthened St. Boniface's mission by naming him an archbishop, and appealed to Charles Martel for help against the Lombards. He was the last pope born outside Europe until Francis in 2013.

sections.h2: Elected by Acclamation at a Funeral
paras: Gregory was born in Syria, the son of a man named John, and was a priest in Rome known for his learning in Greek and Latin and his knowledge of the Psalms. The Roman people acclaimed him as pope during the funeral of Gregory II in February 731. He was consecrated in March after receiving the approval of the exarch in Ravenna; he is generally regarded as the last pope to seek such approval from an imperial representative.

Gregory first sent letters to Emperor Leo III protesting his policy against holy images, but his envoy was detained. In November 731 he held a synod in Rome, attended by many Italian bishops, which decreed excommunication for anyone who removed, destroyed, or profaned images of Christ, the Virgin Mary, the apostles, and the saints.

Leo III retaliated, and at some point confiscated the papal estates in Sicily and southern Italy and is said to have transferred the dioceses of southern Italy and Illyricum from Roman to Constantinopolitan jurisdiction. Historians debate whether these measures came under Gregory III or later. Gregory, for his part, encouraged the veneration of images in Rome, adding icons and decorations to St. Peter's and other churches, including an oratory in St. Peter's honoring the Savior, his Mother, and all the saints.

sections.h2: Archbishop Boniface and the Appeal to Charles Martel
paras: Gregory continued his predecessor's support for St. Boniface, sending him the pallium in 732 and making him an archbishop with authority to create new dioceses in Germany. Boniface visited Rome in 737–738, and Gregory sent him back with further authority as papal legate.

Closer to home, the Lombard king Liutprand seized several towns of the Roman duchy in 739. Gregory allied with the Lombard dukes of Spoleto and Benevento, rebuilt parts of the walls of Rome and of Civitavecchia, and sent envoys to the Frankish leader Charles Martel, with gifts including the keys of St. Peter's tomb, asking for protection. Charles, then allied with Liutprand, did not intervene, but the appeal foreshadowed the later alliance between the papacy and the Franks. Gregory died on 28 November 741, the same year as Charles Martel and Leo III.

keyFacts: Born in Syria; last pope born outside Europe until Francis (2013)
Roman synod of 731 excommunicated destroyers of holy images
Sent the pallium to St. Boniface (732), making him an archbishop
Appealed to Charles Martel against the Lombards (739)

faqs.question: Why is Gregory III significant in papal history?
faqs.answer: He was the last pope to seek an imperial representative's approval of his election, he firmly condemned iconoclasm, and his appeal to Charles Martel was the first step toward the papacy's later alliance with the Franks.

faqs.question: Who was the next pope born outside Europe after Gregory III?
faqs.answer: Pope Francis, born in Buenos Aires, Argentina, and elected in 2013, nearly thirteen centuries later.

faqs.question: Did Charles Martel help Gregory III against the Lombards?
faqs.answer: No. Charles received the pope's envoys and gifts but, being allied with the Lombard king Liutprand, did not send help. The Frankish alliance came only under his son Pepin.
